correctness.rationale: The radial eigenbasis consists of Fock monomials with moments lambda_j(E)=∫_E e^-t t^j/j!dt. Disk labels decrease with gap g_N=e^-s s^N/N!. Any area-preserving delta removal/addition changes every lambda_j by at most delta; 2delta<g_N therefore guarantees the first N labels remain exactly top N even in infinite spectrum. Then q_N(t)=e^-t Σ_{j<N}t^j/j! has derivative -e^-t t^(N-1)/(N-1)!<0, forcing the unique boundary-nearest removal and addition by rearrangement. Integrating q_N=F_N derivative gives exact deficit; symmetric Taylor expansion yields stated positive coefficient plus O(delta^4). Independent 80 small numerical exchange comparisons corroborated the finite arithmetic.

value.rationale: The prescribed-positive-distance stability optimum for a natural higher-rank spectral isoperimetric problem answers a quantitative refinement singled out in prior work, identifies a rigid optimizer among arbitrary radial measurable sets, and proves an exactly sharp quadratic modulus rather than only qualitative disk maximality.

final_claim: For N>=2 radial area-s Fock Toeplitz symbols at symmetric-difference 2delta from disk (0<delta<e^-s s^N/(2N!)), exact smallest KyFan deficit is 2F_N(s)-F_N(s-delta)-F_N(s+delta), with unique annular boundary exchange and sharp e^-s s^(N-1)/(N-1)! delta².
